additions.reason: The Rebbe explicitly notes the double meaning of 'damim' — blood and money — as a bechina-type parallel. When tamkhei orayta give money (damim=money) to Torah scholars, it parallels the blood (damim=blood) flowing away and returning. This double-meaning IS a bechina: the same word/concept operating in two domains simultaneously.

proposed_edges.proof: דָּמִים תַּרְתֵּי מַשְׁמַע — blood and money share the same word because they share the same spiritual dynamic

additions.source_quote: עִקָּר הַצָּרָה בַּלֵּב, כִּי הַלֵּב יוֹדֵעַ וּמַרְגִּישׁ הַצָּרָה בְּיוֹתֵר... כִּי הַלֵּב מֵבִין
additions.reason: The heart is the central physical node of the blood-flow narrative. While not stated with explicit 'bechina' language, the heart is equated with understanding (mevin) and is the seat of the tzarah. It could be added as a node connecting to the tahaluchot hadamim cluster. However, the Rebbe uses it more as a physical description than an explicit bechina declaration, so this is a borderline case.

additions.source_quote: וּבְשָׁעָה שֶׁהַלֵּב בְּצָרָה גַּם הָרֵאָה בְּצָרָה. כִּי הָרֵאָה הִיא קִיּוּם הַגּוּף
additions.reason: The lungs are described in parallel with the heart's distress — when the heart is in trouble, the lungs are too. The shemen (oil) heals the lungs, connecting this to the emet/shemen cluster. However, the Rebbe does not use explicit 'bechina' language for the lungs themselves. Borderline addition.

additions.source_quote: כִּי שַׁבָּת מוֹרָה עַל אֱמוּנַת הַיִּחוּד
additions.reason: Emunot hayichud is explicitly equated with Shabbat — Shabbat demonstrates/teaches the faith in divine unity. This is closely related to 'achdut hapashut' which is already in Package 2, but is stated as a distinct concept.

proposed_edges.proof: שֶׁאָנוּ מַאֲמִינִים, שֶׁכָּל הַפְּעֻלּוֹת מִשְׁתַּנּוֹת נִמְשָׁכִין מֵאֶחָד הַפָּשׁוּט

additions.source_quote: תֻּמֶּיךָ וְאוּרֶיךָ לְאִישׁ חֲסִידֶךָ; שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַחֲסָדִים, דְּהַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת הֲלָכוֹת, נִתְגַלֶּה אוֹר הָאֱמֶת, בְּחִינַת: תֻּמֶּיךָ וְאוּרֶיךָ
additions.reason: Tumekha v'urekha is used as a bechina for the revelation of or ha'emet (light of truth) through chasadim/halakhot. It could be added as a node in the emet cluster.

proposed_edges.proof: נִתְגַלֶּה אוֹר הָאֱמֶת, בְּחִינַת: תֻּמֶּיךָ וְאוּרֶיךָ

additions.source_quote: כִּי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר – הֲלָכָה כְּמוֹתוֹ בְּכָל מָקוֹם... וְהָיָה רוֹצֶה לְהַרְאוֹת, שֶׁזָּכָה לִשְׁלֵמוּת הַדִּבּוּר
additions.reason: R' Eliezer is described as the personality who achieved shlemut hadibbur (completeness of speech). He is the human anchor for the ribua hadibbur concept, similar to how Yaakov and Avraham anchor concepts in Torah #1. Not stated with explicit 'bechina' language but is clearly identified with the dibbur domain.

analysis_notes.critical_dataset_gap: The most significant gap is that the entire dataset for Torah #2 (reference 1002) contains ZERO bechina edges. All 50 edges are classified as eitza or cause. This means the bechina subgraph for this Torah is entirely missing from the dataset. The 71 bechina edges identified in this analysis were all mined directly from the source text. This represents a major classification gap that should be addressed: many of these 'eitza' edges may need to be reclassified, and the 71 bechina edges identified here should be added to the dataset.
